column3: MT 68:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1. Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB renders the word for the place of riding as “through the deserts,” and “in Yah is His name” as “Whose name is the LORD”; NASB supplies “a song.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “causes to dwell in a household” is rendered “makes a home.”
Close to the Hebrew; “in a desolate place” is rendered “through the wilderness.”
NASB supplies “rain” and “quaked,” and renders “this Sinai” as “Sinai itself.”
“Rain of free offerings” is rendered “a plentiful rain,” and “weary” as “parched.”
“Your community” is rendered “Your creatures.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a word” is rendered “the command,” and “the women who bear news” as “The women who proclaim the good tidings.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the beauty of the house” is rendered “she who remains at home.” NASB sets the verse as a quotation.
“Between the saddlebags” is rendered “among the sheepfolds,” and NASB supplies “You are like.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Let it snow” is rendered “It was snowing”; the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew is a series of addresses, “O mountain of God, mountain of Bashan”; NASB renders them as statements.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Twice ten thousand, thousands of repetition” is rendered “myriads, thousands upon thousands,” and NASB supplies “as at.”
Close to the Hebrew; “you took gifts among humankind” is rendered “You have received gifts among men,” and “Yah God” as “the LORD God.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He carries a load for us” is rendered “who daily bears our burden.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Yahweh the Lord” is rendered “GOD the Lord.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “them.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “in the holy place” is rendered “into the sanctuary.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “Even” and “you who are.”
“Their heap (of stones)” is rendered “in their throng,” and “insignificant” as “the youngest.”
Close to the Hebrew; “be strong” is rendered “Show Yourself strong.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from Your temple” is rendered “Because of Your temple.”
The Hebrew is obscure; NASB renders “bulls,” “Trampling under foot the pieces of silver,” and “He has scattered.” The meaning is uncertain.
